title: Prompt, stream, tool call, permission, approve, result, done
description: Sections 8-10. A prompt runs a command; the agent asks permission; the client approves; the command's output and the reply stream back; the turn ends with its usage.

steps.note: Open a connection to the host (through its relay, or on the LAN).
The first frame is host/hello: the versions this client speaks and the device credential from pairing.
The host picks 0.1 and says which device this connection is. `info` is the same object host/info returns.
ACP starts every agent channel with initialize. The host answers it itself with the agent's capabilities; the client's are not passed on.
ACP protocol version 1. No sign-in methods: the agent runs under its owner's own sign-in on the host.
ACP session/new, unchanged. cwd is the agent's folder from host/agents; a remote client can't pick another folder or add MCP servers that run commands.
The agent's own session id and modes. This connection is now attached to the session.
ACP session/prompt, unchanged. The fake agent runs whatever follows `run: `.
host/turn: a turn started in this session, sent to every attached connection. The turn id ties later notices to it.
ACP session/update, unchanged: the agent announces the tool call.
host/pending_update goes to every connection of every device, attached or not, so an inbox can show it.
ACP session/request_permission, unchanged, as a request from the host on this agent channel.
The client approves with the ACP response, choosing one of the agent's options.
Everyone is told it was answered, and by which device. The first answer wins.
The agent's reply streams as message chunks.
ACP's answer to session/prompt ends the turn for the client that sent it.
host/turn ended, to every attached connection, with this turn's usage.
